data.description:
Found by comparing rebar's DC adapter against mature OSS Jira integrations.

## Finding

Jira DC has built-in rate limiting (Administration -> System -> Rate limiting), introduced in **8.6**,
**Data Center only** (not the old Server edition), and **OFF BY DEFAULT** — an administrator enables
it. It is a per-user TOKEN BUCKET with a fill rate, not a fixed window.

Two consequences for rebar:

1. **A static pacing policy is not implementable.** Because the limit is admin-configured and may be
   absent entirely (pre-8.6, Server edition, or simply disabled), rebar cannot hardcode a rate. The
   entire fix is: read the rate-limit headers WHEN PRESENT, and degrade gracefully when absent.
2. **Atlassian prescribes a specific client behaviour** — sleep `retry-after` seconds PLUS random
   jitter of up to 20%. Worth matching exactly rather than reusing rebar's existing ADR-0036 backoff
   curve, which was designed for a different failure shape.

Also relevant: rate-limit headers are only returned for AUTHENTICATED requests. rebar is always
authenticated so this is fine — but it is another reason a silently-expired PAT degrades into an
opaque failure rather than a clear 401.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the DC transport honours `retry-after` when present, with up to 20% random jitter, per
      Atlassian's documented guidance
- [ ] absence of rate-limit headers is handled as NORMAL (disabled / pre-8.6 / Server), not as an error
- [ ] a test drives both paths: headers present, and headers absent
- [ ] the divergence from ADR-0036's backoff curve is documented with the reason
data.title: DC rate-limit headers are not honoured; retry policy cannot be static
